title: Personal Credit Cards: Receiving Account for a Closing Points Cash-Out
content:
This page of the Personal Credit Cards rewards terms settles which account the cash from a closing cash-out goes into, and how that differs from deposits made at other times.

## Rule

- Cash from a closing cash-out can go only to a checking account at PCB that the cardholder owns and that is in active status. Taking points into savings, onto the card as a credit, as a gift card or as travel is not a closing cash-out.
- While money will remain owed on the closed card, the receiving account is the checking account from which the card's automatic payment is to collect that remaining debt after the closing, that is, the autopay source recorded on the card, so that the value of the points arrives where the debt is drawn from. A card whose recorded autopay source is missing, is not the cardholder's own PCB checking account, or is not active has no receiving account, and no points are cashed out.
- Where nothing will remain owed, the cash goes to whichever of their own active PCB checking accounts the cardholder chooses.
- A cardholder without any active checking account at PCB cannot take a closing cash-out.
- When no closing is involved, points may still be paid as a deposit into a checking or a savings account at PCB held by that same customer, valued at the tier's cash worth per point.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical)

| Money will remain owed | Account concerned | Receiving account |
|---|---|---|
| yes | autopay source recorded on the card: the cardholder's own checking, active | that checking account |
| yes | no autopay source recorded on the card | none, nothing is cashed out |
| yes | autopay source recorded on the card: the cardholder's own checking, dormant | none, nothing is cashed out |
| no | the cardholder names their own active checking | that checking account |
| no | the cardholder names their own savings account | not acceptable for a closing cash-out |

A cardholder who, outside any closing, asks for points to go into an active savings account of their own is not barred by these limits, which reach only a closing cash-out.
